description: Define core domain types and enums: It exposes id, policy_id, claim_type (one of MOTOR|HEALTH|LIFE), incident_date, claim_amount (Decimal), status, and a nullable parent_claim_id.
steps: Set up: The Claim type definition.
Action: Inspected.
Assert: It exposes id, policy_id, claim_type (one of MOTOR|HEALTH|LIFE), incident_date, claim_amount (Decimal), status, and a nullable parent_claim_id.

description: Define core domain types and enums: It contains exactly INTAKE, DOCS_PENDING, FRAUD_SCREENING, ASSESSMENT, AUTO_APPROVED, MANUAL_REVIEW, REJECTED, SETTLED, REOPENED, PROCESSING_FAILED.
steps: Set up: The ClaimStatus enum.
Action: Enumerated.
Assert: It contains exactly INTAKE, DOCS_PENDING, FRAUD_SCREENING, ASSESSMENT, AUTO_APPROVED, MANUAL_REVIEW, REJECTED, SETTLED, REOPENED, PROCESSING_FAILED.

description: Define core domain types and enums: It contains exactly CUSTOMER, ASSESSOR, ADMIN.
steps: Set up: The Role enum.
Action: Enumerated.
Assert: It contains exactly CUSTOMER, ASSESSOR, ADMIN.

description: Define core domain types and enums: It exposes policy_number, product_type, status (ACTIVE|LAPSED|...), sum_insured (Decimal), effective_date, expiry_date.
steps: Set up: The Policy type.
Action: Inspected.
Assert: It exposes policy_number, product_type, status (ACTIVE|LAPSED|...), sum_insured (Decimal), effective_date, expiry_date.

description: Define core domain types and enums: It is a fixed-point Decimal type, never a floating-point float (NFR-01).
steps: Set up: Any monetary field across Claim, Assessment, and Settlement.
Action: Its declared type is inspected.
Assert: It is a fixed-point Decimal type, never a floating-point float (NFR-01).

description: Build the claim state machine transition gate: The claim status becomes FRAUD_SCREENING.
steps: Set up: A claim in DOCS_PENDING and event DOCS_VERIFIED.
Action: Transition() is called.
Assert: The claim status becomes FRAUD_SCREENING.

description: Build the claim state machine transition gate: It raises InvalidClaimStateException and the claim status is unchanged.
steps: Set up: A claim in SETTLED and event SUBMIT_FNOL (an invalid transition for that state).
Action: Transition() is called.
Assert: It raises InvalidClaimStateException and the claim status is unchanged.

description: Build the claim state machine transition gate: Each appears as a key with an explicit set of valid outgoing events and no implicit fallthrough.
steps: Set up: The transition table.
Action: Every ClaimStatus value is checked.
Assert: Each appears as a key with an explicit set of valid outgoing events and no implicit fallthrough.

description: Build the claim state machine transition gate: A ClaimStateTransition record (from_state, to_state, event, timestamp) is returned for the caller to persist.
steps: Set up: A successful transition.
Action: It completes.
Assert: A ClaimStateTransition record (from_state, to_state, event, timestamp) is returned for the caller to persist.

description: Define reason codes and domain exceptions: It contains exactly POLICY_INACTIVE, ZERO_PAYABLE_AMOUNT, FRAUD_FLAG, AUTO_APPROVED_LOW_RISK, HIGH_VALUE_REVIEW, DOCS_INCOMPLETE.
steps: Set up: The ReasonCode enum.
Action: Enumerated.
Assert: It contains exactly POLICY_INACTIVE, ZERO_PAYABLE_AMOUNT, FRAUD_FLAG, AUTO_APPROVED_LOW_RISK, HIGH_VALUE_REVIEW, DOCS_INCOMPLETE.

description: Define reason codes and domain exceptions: It carries the policy_number and incident_date that failed validation.
steps: Set up: PolicyNotActiveException.
Action: Raised.
Assert: It carries the policy_number and incident_date that failed validation.

description: Define reason codes and domain exceptions: It carries the policy_number and incident_date of the conflicting claim.
steps: Set up: DuplicateClaimException.
Action: Raised.
Assert: It carries the policy_number and incident_date of the conflicting claim.

description: Define reason codes and domain exceptions: Its type maps to exactly one HTTP status code (409 for duplicate, 422 for policy-inactive, 409 for invalid transition).
steps: Set up: Any domain exception in this module.
Action: Caught by the API layer.
Assert: Its type maps to exactly one HTTP status code (409 for duplicate, 422 for policy-inactive, 409 for invalid transition).

description: Load fraud rule configuration from declarative config: It contains exactly 5 rules matching BRD section 11 weights: ratio>0.8 (+40), filed within 3 days (+25), more than 2 claims in 90 days (+30), motor missing FIR (+15), round number divisible by 10000 (+10).
steps: Set up: Config/fraud-rules.json.
Action: Loaded at startup.

Assert: It contains exactly 5 rules matching BRD section 11 weights: ratio>0.8 (+40), filed within 3 days (+25), more than 2 claims in 90 days (+30), motor missing FIR (+15), round number divisible by 10000 (+10).

description: Load fraud rule configuration from declarative config: Its value is 60.
steps: Set up: The loaded config.
Action: The flag threshold is read.
Assert: Its value is 60.

description: Load fraud rule configuration from declarative config: It raises a typed config error at startup rather than the app starting with silent defaults.
steps: Set up: The config loader.
Action: The file is missing or malformed.
Assert: It raises a typed config error at startup rather than the app starting with silent defaults.

description: Load fraud rule configuration from declarative config: The fraud service picks up the new value on next load.
steps: Set up: The threshold value.
Action: Changed in the config file only with no code change.
Assert: The fraud service picks up the new value on next load.

description: Load deductible, co-pay, and decision threshold configuration: Motor has deductible 5000 and co_pay_pct 0, health has deductible 1000 and co_pay_pct 10, life has deductible 0 and co_pay_pct 0.
steps: Set up: Config/assessment-rules.json.
Action: Loaded.
Assert: Motor has deductible 5000 and co_pay_pct 0, health has deductible 1000 and co_pay_pct 10, life has deductible 0 and co_pay_pct 0.

description: Load deductible, co-pay, and decision threshold configuration: Auto_approve_ceiling equals 50000.
steps: Set up: The decision config.
Action: Loaded.
Assert: Auto_approve_ceiling equals 50000.

description: Load deductible, co-pay, and decision threshold configuration: The loader raises a typed UnknownClaimTypeError.
steps: Set up: The config.
Action: A claim_type outside {motor, health, life} is requested.
Assert: The loader raises a typed UnknownClaimTypeError.

description: Centralize application and role configuration: It exposes db_path, backend_port (8000), and frontend_port (5173).
steps: Set up: AppConfig.
Action: Loaded.
Assert: It exposes db_path, backend_port (8000), and frontend_port (5173).

description: Centralize application and role configuration: It equals exactly CUSTOMER, ASSESSOR, ADMIN, matching the Role enum in Types.
steps: Set up: AppConfig.valid_roles.
Action: Enumerated.
Assert: It equals exactly CUSTOMER, ASSESSOR, ADMIN, matching the Role enum in Types.

description: Centralize application and role configuration: It raises a typed config error naming the missing variable.
steps: Set up: A missing required environment variable with no default.
Action: AppConfig loads.
Assert: It raises a typed config error naming the missing variable.

description: Write append-only numbered SQLite migrations: Every file matches NNNN_description.sql and NNNN is strictly increasing with no gaps.
steps: Set up: The migrations/ directory.
Action: Listed.
Assert: Every file matches NNNN_description.sql and NNNN is strictly increasing with no gaps.

description: Write append-only numbered SQLite migrations: All 9 tables exist: policies, claims, claim_documents, fraud_screenings, assessments, decisions, settlements, claim_state_transitions, admin_overrides.
steps: Set up: A fresh SQLite file.
Action: The migration runner executes.
Assert: All 9 tables exist: policies, claims, claim_documents, fraud_screenings, assessments, decisions, settlements, claim_state_transitions, admin_overrides.

description: Write append-only numbered SQLite migrations: It is idempotent: already-applied migrations are skipped with no error.
steps: Set up: The migration runner.
Action: Run twice against the same database.
Assert: It is idempotent: already-applied migrations are skipped with no error.

description: Write append-only numbered SQLite migrations: A mismatch, indicating a post-application edit, raises a startup error.
steps: Set up: An already-applied migration file.
Action: Its checksum is recomputed at startup.
Assert: A mismatch, indicating a post-application edit, raises a startup error.

description: Build the policy repository: It returns the Policy with matching sum_insured and dates.
steps: Set up: A seeded active policy.
Action: Get_by_number() is called.
Assert: It returns the Policy with matching sum_insured and dates.

description: Build the policy repository: It returns None rather than raising, so the caller can produce a domain-level error.
steps: Set up: A policy number that does not exist.
Action: Get_by_number() is called.
Assert: It returns None rather than raising, so the caller can produce a domain-level error.

description: Build the policy repository: It returns False.
steps: Set up: A policy.
Action: Is_active_on(date) is called with a date outside [effective_date, expiry_date].
Assert: It returns False.

description: Build the claim repository: A row is inserted with status='INTAKE' and the generated id is returned.
steps: Set up: A new claim payload.
Action: Create() is called.
Assert: A row is inserted with status='INTAKE' and the generated id is returned.

description: Build the claim repository: The row's status column is updated and a claim_state_transitions row is inserted in the same transaction.
steps: Set up: An existing claim and a valid event from the E1-S2 transition table.
Action: Apply_transition() is called.
Assert: The row's status column is updated and a claim_state_transitions row is inserted in the same transaction.

description: Build the claim repository: No row is mutated and InvalidClaimStateException propagates.
steps: Set up: An existing claim and an invalid event.
Action: Apply_transition() is called.
Assert: No row is mutated and InvalidClaimStateException propagates.

description: Build the claim repository: Only matching rows are returned.
steps: Set up: Claims of mixed status and product.
Action: List_by_status_and_product() is called with filters.
Assert: Only matching rows are returned.

description: Build the claim repository: It returns True.
steps: Set up: A policy_number and incident_date matching an existing non-void claim.
Action: Exists_duplicate() is called.
Assert: It returns True.

description: Build the append-only audit repositories: Both rows persist with history preserved and no overwrite.
steps: Set up: A FraudScreening record.
Action: Insert() is called twice for the same claim.
Assert: Both rows persist with history preserved and no overwrite.

description: Build the append-only audit repositories: It exposes no update() or delete() method for any of the five entities.
steps: Set up: The repository module.
Action: Its public interface is inspected.
Assert: It exposes no update() or delete() method for any of the five entities.

description: Build the append-only audit repositories: It returns the most recently inserted Assessment row for that claim.
steps: Set up: A claim id.
Action: Get_latest_assessment() is called.
Assert: It returns the most recently inserted Assessment row for that claim.

description: Build the append-only audit repositories: It returns all override rows ordered by timestamp ascending.
steps: Set up: A claim id.
Action: List_admin_overrides() is called.
Assert: It returns all override rows ordered by timestamp ascending.

description: Implement the FNOL intake service: A Claim is created with claim_type='MOTOR' and two ClaimDocument rows (POLICE_FIR, INVOICE) each MISSING.
steps: Set up: A valid motor FNOL payload.
Action: Submit_fnol() is called.
Assert: A Claim is created with claim_type='MOTOR' and two ClaimDocument rows (POLICE_FIR, INVOICE) each MISSING.

description: Implement the FNOL intake service: The checklist rows are exactly HOSPITAL_BILL and DISCHARGE_SUMMARY.
steps: Set up: A valid health FNOL payload.
Action: Submitted.
Assert: The checklist rows are exactly HOSPITAL_BILL and DISCHARGE_SUMMARY.

description: Implement the FNOL intake service: The checklist row is exactly DEATH_CERTIFICATE.
steps: Set up: A valid life FNOL payload.
Action: Submitted.
Assert: The checklist row is exactly DEATH_CERTIFICATE.

description: Implement the FNOL intake service: The claim's initial status is INTAKE and, once checklist rows are attached, it transitions to DOCS_PENDING.
steps: Set up: A successful submission.
Action: It completes.
Assert: The claim's initial status is INTAKE and, once checklist rows are attached, it transitions to DOCS_PENDING.

description: Enforce policy-active validation at incident date: PolicyNotActiveException is raised and no Claim row is created.
steps: Set up: A policy with status='LAPSED'.
Action: Submit_fnol() is called referencing it.
Assert: PolicyNotActiveException is raised and no Claim row is created.

description: Enforce policy-active validation at incident date: PolicyNotActiveException is raised.
steps: Set up: An active policy but an incident_date after expiry_date.
Action: Submitted.
Assert: PolicyNotActiveException is raised.

description: Enforce policy-active validation at incident date: No exception is raised and intake proceeds.
steps: Set up: An active policy with incident_date within [effective_date, expiry_date].
Action: Submitted.
Assert: No exception is raised and intake proceeds.

description: Enforce policy-active validation at incident date: The response uses reason code POLICY_INACTIVE.
steps: Set up: PolicyNotActiveException reaches the API layer.
Action: Serialized.
Assert: The response uses reason code POLICY_INACTIVE.

description: Detect and reject duplicate FNOL submissions: DuplicateClaimException is raised and no new Claim row is created.
steps: Set up: An existing non-void claim for policy P on date D.
Action: A second FNOL for (P, D) is submitted.
Assert: DuplicateClaimException is raised and no new Claim row is created.

description: Detect and reject duplicate FNOL submissions: It succeeds and creates a second, independent claim.
steps: Set up: An existing claim for policy P on date D1.
Action: A new FNOL for (P, D2) with D2 not equal to D1 is submitted.
Assert: It succeeds and creates a second, independent claim.

description: Detect and reject duplicate FNOL submissions: The HTTP response status is 409.
steps: Set up: DuplicateClaimException reaches the API layer.
Action: Serialized.
Assert: The HTTP response status is 409.

description: Enforce the per-claim-type document checklist: It returns False and the claim remains DOCS_PENDING.
steps: Set up: A motor claim with POLICE_FIR still MISSING.
Action: Check_documents_complete() is called.
Assert: It returns False and the claim remains DOCS_PENDING.

description: Enforce the per-claim-type document checklist: It returns True and the claim transitions to FRAUD_SCREENING.
steps: Set up: A motor claim with both POLICE_FIR and INVOICE set to VERIFIED.
Action: Checked.
Assert: It returns True and the claim transitions to FRAUD_SCREENING.

description: Enforce the per-claim-type document checklist: Only HOSPITAL_BILL and DISCHARGE_SUMMARY are considered, ignoring motor/life document types.
steps: Set up: A health claim.
Action: Its checklist is evaluated.
Assert: Only HOSPITAL_BILL and DISCHARGE_SUMMARY are considered, ignoring motor/life document types.

description: Enforce the per-claim-type document checklist: It raises a typed validation error.
steps: Set up: An attempt to mark a document type that is not part of the claim's own claim-type checklist.
Action: Verify_document() is called.
Assert: It raises a typed validation error.

description: Implement the deterministic fraud scoring engine: The total is 40 and flagged is False, since 40 is below threshold 60.
steps: Set up: A claim with a claim_amount/sum_insured ratio of 0.85 and no other rule triggers.
Action: Scored.
Assert: The total is 40 and flagged is False, since 40 is below threshold 60.

description: Implement the deterministic fraud scoring engine: The total is 65 (40+25) and flagged is True.
steps: Set up: A claim filed 2 days after policy inception with a claim_amount/sum_insured ratio of 0.85.
Action: Scored.
Assert: The total is 65 (40+25) and flagged is True.

description: Implement the deterministic fraud scoring engine: Both runs produce an identical score and rule breakdown, demonstrating determinism.
steps: Set up: The same claim inputs scored twice.
Action: The two results are compared.
Assert: Both runs produce an identical score and rule breakdown, demonstrating determinism.

description: Implement the deterministic fraud scoring engine: The +15 rule is included in the breakdown with its rule name.
steps: Set up: A motor claim missing the POLICE_FIR document.
Action: Scored.
Assert: The +15 rule is included in the breakdown with its rule name.

description: Persist fraud screenings and gate the pipeline: The FraudScreening row stores the threshold that was active at scoring time, not the current config value.
steps: Set up: A scored claim.
Action: The result is persisted.
Assert: The FraudScreening row stores the threshold that was active at scoring time, not the current config value.

description: Persist fraud screenings and gate the pipeline: The claim moves toward MANUAL_REVIEW with reason code FRAUD_FLAG.
steps: Set up: A flagged=True result.
Action: Persisted.
Assert: The claim moves toward MANUAL_REVIEW with reason code FRAUD_FLAG.

description: Persist fraud screenings and gate the pipeline: The claim moves toward ASSESSMENT.
steps: Set up: A flagged=False result.
Action: Persisted.
Assert: The claim moves toward ASSESSMENT.

description: Persist fraud screenings and gate the pipeline: Both rows remain independently queryable with no overwrite, per NFR-02.
steps: Set up: Two screenings on the same claim, for example after a retry.
Action: Both are persisted.
Assert: Both rows remain independently queryable with no overwrite, per NFR-02.

description: Implement the assessment service: Payable_amount equals 35000 (40000 minus the 5000 deductible, no co-pay).
steps: Set up: A motor claim with claim_amount 40000 and sum_insured 100000.
Action: Assessed.
Assert: Payable_amount equals 35000 (40000 minus the 5000 deductible, no co-pay).

description: Implement the assessment service: The 1000 deductible and 10% co-pay of 19000 (=1900) yield payable_amount 17100.
steps: Set up: A health claim with claim_amount 20000.
Action: Assessed.
Assert: The 1000 deductible and 10% co-pay of 19000 (=1900) yield payable_amount 17100.

description: Implement the assessment service: Payable_amount equals min(200000,150000) = 150000 with no deductions.
steps: Set up: A life claim with claim_amount 200000 and sum_insured 150000.
Action: Assessed.
Assert: Payable_amount equals min(200000,150000) = 150000 with no deductions.

description: Implement the assessment service: Payable_amount is clamped to 0 and is never negative.
steps: Set up: Inputs that would mathematically compute negative.
Action: Assessed.
Assert: Payable_amount is clamped to 0 and is never negative.

description: Implement the assessment service: Payable_amount is a Decimal and the computation used no float arithmetic at any step.
steps: Set up: Any assessment result.
Action: Its type is inspected.
Assert: Payable_amount is a Decimal and the computation used no float arithmetic at any step.

description: Implement the decision engine: The outcome is REJECT with reason code ZERO_PAYABLE_AMOUNT.
steps: Set up: Payable_amount == 0.
Action: Decided.
Assert: The outcome is REJECT with reason code ZERO_PAYABLE_AMOUNT.

description: Implement the decision engine: The outcome is MANUAL_REVIEW with reason code FRAUD_FLAG.
steps: Set up: A fraud-flagged claim with nonzero payable_amount.
Action: Decided.
Assert: The outcome is MANUAL_REVIEW with reason code FRAUD_FLAG.

description: Implement the decision engine: The outcome is AUTO_APPROVE with reason code AUTO_APPROVED_LOW_RISK.
steps: Set up: An unflagged claim with payable_amount of 30000, at or below the 50000 ceiling.
Action: Decided.
Assert: The outcome is AUTO_APPROVE with reason code AUTO_APPROVED_LOW_RISK.

description: Implement the decision engine: The outcome is MANUAL_REVIEW with reason code HIGH_VALUE_REVIEW.
steps: Set up: An unflagged claim with payable_amount of 75000, above the ceiling.
Action: Decided.
Assert: The outcome is MANUAL_REVIEW with reason code HIGH_VALUE_REVIEW.

description: Implement the decision engine: The Decision row is append-only and records decided_by as either 'system' or an assessor actor id.
steps: Set up: A decision result.
Action: Persisted.
Assert: The Decision row is append-only and records decided_by as either 'system' or an assessor actor id.

description: Orchestrate the claim pipeline with failure handling: It ends in exactly one terminal state among AUTO_APPROVED, MANUAL_REVIEW, REJECTED, with a matching Decision row.
steps: Set up: A claim with complete documents and no fraud flag.
Action: Run_pipeline() is invoked.
Assert: It ends in exactly one terminal state among AUTO_APPROVED, MANUAL_REVIEW, REJECTED, with a matching Decision row.

description: Orchestrate the claim pipeline with failure handling: It halts at DOCS_PENDING and does not call the fraud or assessment services.
steps: Set up: A claim with incomplete documents.
Action: Run_pipeline() is invoked.
Assert: It halts at DOCS_PENDING and does not call the fraud or assessment services.

description: Orchestrate the claim pipeline with failure handling: The claim transitions to PROCESSING_FAILED and the error is logged as structured JSON with no PII fields, per NFR-06.
steps: Set up: The fraud or assessment step raises an unexpected exception.
Action: Caught by the orchestrator.
Assert: The claim transitions to PROCESSING_FAILED and the error is logged as structured JSON with no PII fields, per NFR-06.

description: Orchestrate the claim pipeline with failure handling: The pipeline re-runs starting from the failed step.
steps: Set up: A claim in PROCESSING_FAILED.
Action: An admin calls retry_pipeline().
Assert: The pipeline re-runs starting from the failed step.

description: Implement the settlement service: A Settlement row is created with the decision's payable_amount and the claim transitions to SETTLED.
steps: Set up: A decision outcome of AUTO_APPROVE.
Action: Settlement runs.
Assert: A Settlement row is created with the decision's payable_amount and the claim transitions to SETTLED.

description: Implement the settlement service: No update method exists, since the repository (E3-S4) enforces immutability.
steps: Set up: A created Settlement row.
Action: Any code path attempts to modify it.
Assert: No update method exists, since the repository (E3-S4) enforces immutability.

description: Implement the settlement service: It returns a stub confirmation reference without contacting any real external payment rail.
steps: Set up: Settlement completes.
Action: The stubbed payment trigger is invoked.
Assert: It returns a stub confirmation reference without contacting any real external payment rail.

description: Implement the settlement service: It is refused with a typed error and no Settlement row is created for a non-approved claim.
steps: Set up: A REJECTED claim.
Action: Settlement is attempted.
Assert: It is refused with a typed error and no Settlement row is created for a non-approved claim.

description: Implement the reopen/dispute service: A new Claim row is created with parent_claim_id set to the original's id and status='INTAKE'.
steps: Set up: A SETTLED claim.
Action: Reopen() is called.
Assert: A new Claim row is created with parent_claim_id set to the original's id and status='INTAKE'.

description: Implement the reopen/dispute service: Its historical Decision, Settlement, and Assessment rows are unchanged: still readable, not deleted or edited.
steps: Set up: The reopen call succeeds.
Action: The original claim is re-read.
Assert: Its historical Decision, Settlement, and Assessment rows are unchanged: still readable, not deleted or edited.

description: Implement the reopen/dispute service: It is REOPENED, having been set via the state-machine gate rather than a direct column write.
steps: Set up: The reopen call succeeds.
Action: The original claim's status is re-read.
Assert: It is REOPENED, having been set via the state-machine gate rather than a direct column write.

description: Implement the reopen/dispute service: It raises InvalidClaimStateException.
steps: Set up: A claim that is not SETTLED, for example one in MANUAL_REVIEW.
Action: Reopen() is called.
Assert: It raises InvalidClaimStateException.

description: Implement the stubbed role-based auth dependency: The route handler receives an ActorContext with role=ASSESSOR and the given actor_id.
steps: Set up: A request with X-Role: ASSESSOR and a valid actor id.
Action: The dependency resolves.
Assert: The route handler receives an ActorContext with role=ASSESSOR and the given actor_id.

description: Implement the stubbed role-based auth dependency: The request is rejected with HTTP 401 before the route handler runs.
steps: Set up: A request with X-Role: SUPERVISOR, a value not in valid_roles.
Action: The dependency resolves.
Assert: The request is rejected with HTTP 401 before the route handler runs.

description: Implement the stubbed role-based auth dependency: It is rejected with HTTP 401.
steps: Set up: A request missing the X-Role header entirely.
Action: The dependency resolves.
Assert: It is rejected with HTTP 401.

description: Implement the stubbed role-based auth dependency: It is rejected with HTTP 403.
steps: Set up: A route decorated with require_role(ADMIN).
Action: A request arrives with X-Role: ASSESSOR.
Assert: It is rejected with HTTP 403.

description: Implement the admin override service: An AdminOverride row is inserted recording the admin actor, command, reason_code, and timestamp.
steps: Set up: An admin actor and a target claim.
Action: Override() is called with a command and reason code.
Assert: An AdminOverride row is inserted recording the admin actor, command, reason_code, and timestamp.

description: Implement the admin override service: It raises a typed validation error and no override row is inserted.
steps: Set up: Override() is called without a reason_code.
Action: Validated.
Assert: It raises a typed validation error and no override row is inserted.

description: Implement the admin override service: The status change goes through the E1-S2 transition gate, and an invalid target status raises InvalidClaimStateException.
steps: Set up: An override that changes claim status.
Action: Applied.
Assert: The status change goes through the E1-S2 transition gate, and an invalid target status raises InvalidClaimStateException.

description: Implement the admin override service: It fails with InvalidClaimStateException rather than silently double-applying, per BRD section 11 concurrency handling.
steps: Set up: Two admins concurrently overriding the same claim.
Action: The second call runs against the now-stale state.
Assert: It fails with InvalidClaimStateException rather than silently double-applying, per BRD section 11 concurrency handling.

description: Expose the claims API for intake, tracking, and dispute: The response is 201 with a body containing the new claim_id and initial status.
steps: Set up: A valid motor FNOL body.
Action: POST /api/claims is called with X-Role: CUSTOMER.
Assert: The response is 201 with a body containing the new claim_id and initial status.

description: Expose the claims API for intake, tracking, and dispute: The response is 409 with reason_code DUPLICATE_CLAIM.
steps: Set up: A duplicate FNOL.
Action: Submitted.
Assert: The response is 409 with reason_code DUPLICATE_CLAIM.

description: Expose the claims API for intake, tracking, and dispute: The response is 201 with the new sub-claim's id and parent_claim_id.
steps: Set up: A SETTLED claim id.
Action: POST /api/claims/{id}/reopen is called.
Assert: The response is 201 with the new sub-claim's id and parent_claim_id.

description: Expose the claims API for intake, tracking, and dispute: The response body includes status, decision.reason_codes if decided, and a missing_documents list.
steps: Set up: GET /api/claims/{id} on an existing claim.
Action: Called.
Assert: The response body includes status, decision.reason_codes if decided, and a missing_documents list.

description: Expose the document verification API: The response lists only claims currently in DOCS_PENDING with their outstanding document types.
steps: Set up: X-Role: ASSESSOR.
Action: GET /api/claims/documents/pending is called.
Assert: The response lists only claims currently in DOCS_PENDING with their outstanding document types.

description: Expose the document verification API: The response reflects the update and, once all items are verified, a follow-up GET shows the claim's status as FRAUD_SCREENING.
steps: Set up: A claim's POLICE_FIR document.
Action: PATCH /api/claims/{id}/documents/{type} sets it to VERIFIED.
Assert: The response reflects the update and, once all items are verified, a follow-up GET shows the claim's status as FRAUD_SCREENING.

description: Expose the document verification API: The response is 403.
steps: Set up: X-Role: CUSTOMER.
Action: The same PATCH endpoint is called.
Assert: The response is 403.

description: Expose the assessor workbench API: The response lists only claims whose latest FraudScreening.flagged is True.
steps: Set up: X-Role: ASSESSOR.
Action: GET /api/claims/fraud-alerts is called.
Assert: The response lists only claims whose latest FraudScreening.flagged is True.

description: Expose the assessor workbench API: The response includes the fraud score and breakdown, the assessed payable_amount, and decision-rationale fields.
steps: Set up: A claim in MANUAL_REVIEW.
Action: GET /api/claims/{id}/workbench is called.
Assert: The response includes the fraud score and breakdown, the assessed payable_amount, and decision-rationale fields.

description: Expose the assessor workbench API: The response is 200 and a new append-only Decision row is created with decided_by set to the assessor's actor id.
steps: Set up: A claim in MANUAL_REVIEW.
Action: POST /api/claims/{id}/decision is called with an assessor's outcome and reason code.
Assert: The response is 200 and a new append-only Decision row is created with decided_by set to the assessor's actor id.

description: Expose the admin API for queues, overrides, and audit trail: Only matching claims are returned.
steps: Set up: X-Role: ADMIN.
Action: GET /api/admin/claims?status=MANUAL_REVIEW&product=MOTOR is called.
Assert: Only matching claims are returned.

description: Expose the admin API for queues, overrides, and audit trail: The response lists every Settlement row with claim id, amount, and timestamp as an immutable audit trail.
steps: Set up: X-Role: ADMIN.
Action: GET /api/admin/payouts is called.
Assert: The response lists every Settlement row with claim id, amount, and timestamp as an immutable audit trail.

description: Expose the admin API for queues, overrides, and audit trail: The response is 200 and the created AdminOverride is visible in a subsequent GET /api/admin/claims/{id}/overrides.
steps: Set up: X-Role: ADMIN.
Action: POST /api/admin/claims/{id}/override is called with a command and reason code.
Assert: The response is 200 and the created AdminOverride is visible in a subsequent GET /api/admin/claims/{id}/overrides.

description: Expose the admin API for queues, overrides, and audit trail: The response is 403.
steps: Set up: X-Role: ASSESSOR, not ADMIN.
Action: Any /api/admin/* endpoint is called.
Assert: The response is 403.

description: Build the FNOL submission form: All fields remain reachable without horizontal scrolling.
steps: Set up: The form loaded at a mobile viewport of 375px wide.
Action: Rendered.
Assert: All fields remain reachable without horizontal scrolling.

description: Build the FNOL submission form: It shows exactly Hospital bill and Discharge summary toggles, not motor or life document labels.
steps: Set up: A claim type of HEALTH selected.
Action: The checklist section renders.
Assert: It shows exactly Hospital bill and Discharge summary toggles, not motor or life document labels.

description: Build the FNOL submission form: An inline validation message appears and no API call is made.
steps: Set up: A submission with a missing required field.
Action: Submit is clicked.
Assert: An inline validation message appears and no API call is made.

description: Build the FNOL submission form: The UI navigates to the claim tracker view for the new claim id.
steps: Set up: A successful submission.
Action: The API returns 201.
Assert: The UI navigates to the claim tracker view for the new claim id.

description: Build the claim tracker view: It lists each outstanding document type distinctly from verified ones.
steps: Set up: A claim in DOCS_PENDING.
Action: The tracker renders.
Assert: It lists each outstanding document type distinctly from verified ones.

description: Build the claim tracker view: The human-readable reason text, not just the raw code, is displayed.
steps: Set up: A claim with outcome MANUAL_REVIEW and reason code HIGH_VALUE_REVIEW.
Action: Rendered.
Assert: The human-readable reason text, not just the raw code, is displayed.

description: Build the claim tracker view: The settled payout amount is displayed and a Dispute this claim action is visible.
steps: Set up: A SETTLED claim.
Action: Rendered.
Assert: The settled payout amount is displayed and a Dispute this claim action is visible.

description: Build the claim tracker view: No dispute action is shown.
steps: Set up: A claim that is not SETTLED.
Action: Rendered.
Assert: No dispute action is shown.

description: Build the dispute action flow: A confirmation dialog appears before any API call is made.
steps: Set up: The Dispute this claim button on a SETTLED claim.
Action: Clicked.
Assert: A confirmation dialog appears before any API call is made.

description: Build the dispute action flow: The UI shows the new sub-claim id and a link to its tracker.
steps: Set up: Confirmation.
Action: The reopen API call succeeds.
Assert: The UI shows the new sub-claim id and a link to its tracker.

description: Build the dispute action flow: A user-facing error message is shown and the original claim's displayed status is unchanged.
steps: Set up: The reopen API call fails, for example with a 409 invalid state.
Action: The error returns.
Assert: A user-facing error message is shown and the original claim's displayed status is unchanged.

description: Build the document verification queue UI: Only claims in DOCS_PENDING appear, grouped or filterable by claim type.
steps: Set up: The queue loaded.
Action: Rendered.
Assert: Only claims in DOCS_PENDING appear, grouped or filterable by claim type.

description: Build the document verification queue UI: That claim disappears from this queue on the next refresh.
steps: Set up: A checklist item toggled to VERIFIED.
Action: The last outstanding item for a claim is verified.
Assert: That claim disappears from this queue on the next refresh.

description: Build the document verification queue UI: The UI does not render the queue and shows an access-denied state instead.
steps: Set up: The queue is accessed under an X-Role: CUSTOMER context.
Action: Requested.
Assert: The UI does not render the queue and shows an access-denied state instead.

description: Build the fraud alert queue UI: Each row shows the fraud score, the triggered rule names, and a link into the assessor workbench for that claim.
steps: Set up: The queue loaded.
Action: Rendered.
Assert: Each row shows the fraud score, the triggered rule names, and a link into the assessor workbench for that claim.

description: Build the fraud alert queue UI: That claim no longer appears.
steps: Set up: A claim's flag is cleared by a later re-screening.
Action: The queue refreshes.
Assert: That claim no longer appears.

description: Build the fraud alert queue UI: The UI does not render the queue and shows an access-denied state instead.
steps: Set up: The queue is accessed under an X-Role: CUSTOMER context.
Action: Requested.
Assert: The UI does not render the queue and shows an access-denied state instead.

description: Build the assessor workbench UI: It displays the fraud score and breakdown alongside the computed payable_amount.
steps: Set up: A claim in MANUAL_REVIEW.
Action: The workbench renders.
Assert: It displays the fraud score and breakdown alongside the computed payable_amount.

description: Build the assessor workbench UI: The UI shows a confirmation and the claim is removed from the pending workbench list.
steps: Set up: The assessor selects an outcome and reason code and submits.
Action: The API call succeeds.
Assert: The UI shows a confirmation and the claim is removed from the pending workbench list.

description: Build the assessor workbench UI: A validation message blocks the call.
steps: Set up: The assessor attempts to submit without selecting an outcome.
Action: Submit is clicked.
Assert: A validation message blocks the call.

description: Build the admin dashboard UI: The claim queue table updates to match without a full page reload.
steps: Set up: The dashboard loaded.
Action: The status/product filters are changed.
Assert: The claim queue table updates to match without a full page reload.

description: Build the admin dashboard UI: Rows are shown in reverse-chronological order and are read-only with no edit controls.
steps: Set up: The payout audit trail section.
Action: Rendered.
Assert: Rows are shown in reverse-chronological order and are read-only with no edit controls.

description: Build the admin dashboard UI: The form blocks submission with a validation message.
steps: Set up: The override action on a selected claim.
Action: Submitted without a reason code.
Assert: The form blocks submission with a validation message.

description: Build the admin dashboard UI: The new override entry appears in that claim's audit history within the dashboard.
steps: Set up: A successful override.
Action: The API confirms it.
Assert: The new override entry appears in that claim's audit history within the dashboard.
